Advancements in Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) have significantly transformed the delivery of healthcare services worldwide. One of the most notable developments is telemedicine, which enables healthcare professionals to provide medical services remotely through digital platforms. Telemedicine leverages web-based systems, mobile technologies, and internet connectivity to overcome geographical barriers, reduce healthcare costs, and improve access to medical services, particularly for underserved and rural populations.

In recent years, the integration of electronic prescription (e-prescription) systems into telemedicine platforms has further enhanced healthcare efficiency and safety. Electronic prescription management systems allow physicians to generate, transmit, and manage prescriptions digitally, reducing errors associated with handwritten prescriptions, improving medication tracking, and enhancing coordination between healthcare providers and pharmacies. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of telemedicine solutions, highlighting the need for secure, reliable, and user-friendly web-based healthcare systems.
Despite these advancements, many healthcare institutions especially in developing countries

still rely heavily on traditional face-to-face consultations and paper-based prescription methods. These approaches present challenges such as long waiting times, limited access to specialists, prescription errors, and poor medical record management.

This project proposes the design and development of a Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Electronic Prescription Management System to address these challenges and improve the overall quality of healthcare delivery.

Access to timely and quality healthcare services remains a major challenge, particularly for patients living in rural and remote areas. Many healthcare systems face shortages of medical professionals, limited healthcare infrastructure, and long travel distances to medical facilities, which often lead to delayed consultations and inadequate patient–doctor interaction. Studies indicate that rural populations frequently experience barriers such as geographic isolation, workforce shortages, and limited healthcare resources, which reduce access to essential medical

In many healthcare facilities, traditional paper-based processes are still widely used to manage prescriptions and patient records. These manual systems are prone to several challenges, including illegible handwriting, prescription duplication, loss of patient records, and difficulties in tracking medication history. Such limitations increase the risk of medication errors and adverse drug interactions, which can compromise patient safety and treatment effectiveness

Furthermore, the absence of integrated digital healthcare systems limits the ability of healthcare providers to offer remote consultations and manage patient information efficiently. Patients often have to travel long distances to healthcare facilities for minor consultations, follow-ups, or prescription renewals, resulting in increased financial costs and inconvenience. Research shows that telemedicine technologies can significantly improve access to healthcare by enabling remote consultations and reducing travel requirements for patients, particularly in underserved communities

In addition, the lack of digital systems for managing prescriptions and patient medical records makes it difficult for healthcare providers to monitor treatment history, track medication usage, and ensure continuity of care
. These challenges highlight the need for improved technological solutions that can enhance healthcare delivery, patient communication, and data management.
Therefore, there is a need for a secure and efficient web-based telemedicine platform
integrated with an electronic prescription management system that enables remote consultations, digital prescription generation, secure patient data storage, and improved

communication between patients, healthcare professionals, and pharmacies. Such a system has the potential to improve healthcare accessibility, reduce prescription errors, and enhance the overall efficiency of healthcare services.

Rural patients represent the primary end-users of the system individuals who face geographical and logistical barriers to accessing timely healthcare services. infrastructure upon which the entire system is built.

This chapter introduced the proposed project on a Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Electronic Prescription Management System. It outlined the background of the study, identified the existing problems in healthcare delivery and prescription management, stated the objectives and research questions, and discussed the scope, limitations, and significance of the study. The chapter also provided an overview of how the remainder of the report is structured.

This chapter presents a review of existing literature relevant to the development of a Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Electronic Prescription Management System. The review examines prior research and related works in the areas of telemedicine, electronic prescription systems, patient health record management, symptom assessment and triage, and referral scheduling in digital health platforms. The purpose of this review is to identify what has already been studied, assess the strengths and gaps in existing systems, and establish a theoretical and empirical basis for the proposed system.

The literature reviewed spans peer-reviewed journal articles, systematic reviews, narrative reviews, and meta-analyses published from 2017 to 2024, drawn from credible databases including PubMed, Annals of Neurology, the Journal of Medical Internet Research (JMIR), Frontiers in Digital Health, the International Journal of Membrane Science and Technology, and the Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA). In recognition of the deployment context of the proposed system, this review gives deliberate emphasis to studies conducted in Zambia and the broader Sub-Saharan African region. The review is structured into four sections: an introduction, a survey of related works, a critical review of those works, and a description of the proposed system arising from identified gaps.

published a systematic review and meta-analysis in the Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA) assessing the effectiveness of electronic medication systems (EMS) in reducing medication error rates and associated harm among hospital inpatients. The review included 18 studies. Consistent evidence across 14 studies confirmed that transitioning from paper-based medication systems to an EMS is likely to reduce medication error rates, particularly prescribing errors. Meta-analysis of three studies reporting changes in administration errors found a significant reduction in error rates (RR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.72–0.83, p = 0.004)
. This provides strong empirical evidence for the inclusion of an electronic prescription management module in the proposed system.

, publishing in the Journal of Family Medicine and Primary Care, demonstrated significant reductions in prescribing errors following e-prescribing system modifications across multiple hospital departments. The Obstetrics and Gynaecology (OB/GYN) department reduced errors from 0.87% to 0.45%, while the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) showed a complete elimination of errors post-implementation. The study concluded that modifications to e-prescribing systems can effectively address specific medication management needs across different care settings
. These findings support the case for developing a dynamic electronic prescription system adaptable to different clinical scenarios within the proposed platform.

, publishing in the Journal of General Internal Medicine, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effect of electronic prescribing strategies on medication errors and harm in hospitals. The meta-analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in overall medication errors (RR: 0.24, 95% CI: 0.13–0.46) with electronic versus paper prescribing strategies. Dosing errors were reduced in 7 (78%) of the 9 studies reporting this outcome
. This meta-analytic evidence provides a compelling quantitative basis for prioritising the electronic prescription feature in the proposed telemedicine platform.

, publishing in Frontiers in Digital Health, investigated the adoption of electronic medical records (EMRs) in developing countries using a multi-state study of the Nigerian healthcare system. The study, which used Davis's Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), found that critical success factors such as end-user awareness, training, and administrative support had a positive impact on the ease of EMR adoption. The researchers concluded that improving awareness will encourage healthcare staff to invest in upgrading themselves in preparation for the adoption of IT innovations critical to improved patient care
. The findings are highly relevant to the proposed system's implementation strategy, particularly in the Zambian healthcare context where digital literacy among healthcare workers may vary.

, citing evidence published in the journal BMJ Health and Care Informatics, noted that integrating telehealth programmes into a hospital's existing EHR infrastructure helps maximise the benefits of telemedicine, as providers already have experience working with the baseline system. The study also warned that establishing a telehealth platform without adequate EHR integration puts patient health information at higher risks to safety and security
. This finding underpins the need for a unified platform in the proposed system that combines telemedicine consultation with securely integrated patient health records.

Based on the gaps identified in the review of related works, this project proposes the development of a Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Integrated Electronic Prescription Management System, specifically designed for deployment in Zambia. The proposed system is designed to address the following specific gaps identified in the literature.

Unlike the majority of existing telemedicine platforms reviewed, which either focus solely on remote consultation or solely on electronic prescribing, the proposed system integrates both functionalities into a single unified web-based platform. Patients can register, request consultations, communicate with doctors via messaging or video conferencing, receive digital prescriptions, and have those prescriptions transmitted directly to registered pharmacies all within one system. This integrated design responds directly to the fragmentation gap confirmed by both the global literature and the Zambian evidence from Asukile et al.
, who noted the absence of electronic medical records as a key limitation in their
In response to the gap identified by Adepoju et al.
regarding EMR adoption challenges in developing countries, and consistent with the digital literacy challenges documented in the Zambian regulatory context

, the proposed system is designed with a simple, accessible user interface that requires minimal digital literacy from both patients and healthcare providers. The platform will be deployable in bandwidth-constrained environments typical of rural Zambia, with lightweight web technologies that do not require high internet speeds to function effectively.

The most distinctive feature of the proposed system, relative to existing platforms in the literature, is the Referral and Appointment Scheduling module, supported by a Symptom Assessment and Triage component. When a patient submits symptoms that a doctor classifies as
that cannot be conclusively assessed or safely prescribed for through remote consultation
clinical decision logic pathway directs the case through the referral module. The doctor uses this module to arrange an in-person appointment for the patient to undergo
the necessary physical examinations or diagnostic tests before a diagnosis or prescription is issued. This feature directly addresses the patient safety gap highlighted by Gellert et al.
, is inspired by the triage accuracy and decision-routing principles demonstrated by Salman et al.
, and responds to the clinical referral patterns observed by Asukile et al.
Furthermore, the proposed system incorporates secure patient health record storage with role-based access control, ensuring that only authorised
access sensitive medical data. This directly addresses the security concerns raised by Mishra et al.
, and is designed to comply with the data security and interoperability standards mandated by Zambia's HPCZ Guidelines and Statutory Instrument 43 of 2023, as documented by Muyunda and Mpundu

In summary, the proposed system builds on the strengths identified in the reviewed literature including the growing body of Zambian telemedicine evidence while filling the critical gaps of integration, accessibility, safety-aware triage, and secure data management. As illustrated in the comparative analysis presented in Table 2.2, the proposed system is the only platform among those reviewed that fully addresses all ten key features necessary for a comprehensive web-based telemedicine solution in Zambia. It is specifically aligned with the Zambia Digital Health Strategy 2022–2026 and the HPCZ Guidelines for telemedicine quality assurance, and is oriented towards improving healthcare accessibility, reducing prescription errors, enhancing communication between patients and providers, and ensuring that patients with ambiguous symptoms are safely referred for appropriate in-person care.

This chapter presents the methodology adopted for the design and development of the Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Electronic Prescription Management System. The chapter outlines the software development methodology selected, the requirements gathering process, a detailed analysis of functional and non-functional requirements, software and hardware design specifications, and a proposed project timeline and budget. The methodology described in this chapter provides a structured and systematic plan that guides the entire development process from conception to deployment, ensuring that the final system meets the objectives identified in Chapter One and addresses the gaps established in the literature review in Chapter Two.
The methodology was selected to suit the iterative and user-centred nature of the proposed system, which involves multiple stakeholder types patients, doctors, and
with distinct interaction requirements. The approach ensures that the system is developed incrementally, with continuous feedback and refinement at each stage of the development cycle

The Agile Software Development Methodology, specifically the Scrum framework, was selected as the development methodology for this project. Agile is an iterative and incremental approach to software development that emphasises flexibility, collaboration, continuous delivery of working software, and rapid response to change

. The Scrum framework organises development into fixed-length iterations called sprints, typically lasting two to four weeks, at the end of which a potentially shippable increment of the software is produced.

The rationale for selecting Agile Scrum over other methodologies such as Waterfall or the Rational Unified Process (RUP) is threefold. First, the proposed system involves multiple user roles patients, doctors, and pharmacists each with evolving requirements that are best captured and refined incrementally rather than defined entirely upfront. Second, Agile allows for early and continuous testing of system modules, which is critical for a healthcare platform where
functional correctness and data security are paramount. Third,
emphasis on working software over comprehensive documentation aligns with the project's need to produce a functioning prototype within the available timeframe
Agile Scrum Process for This Project
The development of the proposed system will be organised into five sprints as follows:
Requirements gathering, stakeholder analysis, system scoping, conceptual framework validation, and project environment setup (XAMPP, VS Code, MySQL).
System architecture design, database schema design, UI wireframes for all three user roles (patient, doctor, pharmacist), and design review.
Frontend development using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React.js. Implementation of user registration, login, and dashboard interfaces for all roles.
Backend development using Node.js and PHP with MySQL. Implementation of consultation, e-prescription, patient records, pharmacy integration, and referral modules.
System integration, functional and non-functional testing, bug fixing, performance optimisation, documentation, and final submission preparation.

Requirements gathering is the process of identifying, documenting, and managing the needs and expectations of all stakeholders involved in the system. This review identified both the features that existing systems offer and the gaps that the proposed system must address

Use Case Analysis: Use cases were developed to map out the interactions between each user role and the system, identifying the specific actions each user must be able to perform and the system responses expected.
Scenario-Based Analysis: Representative scenarios were constructed to simulate how a patient, doctor, or pharmacist would interact with the platform during a typical telemedicine

The software design specifications describe the architectural structure, data models, and interface designs that will guide the implementation of the proposed system. The design is guided by the principle of separation of concerns and follows a client-server architecture in which the client-side (frontend) and server-side (backend) are developed as distinct but interconnected layers.
The proposed system follows a three-tier client-server architecture consisting of the following layers:

Presentation Layer (Frontend): Built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React.js, the presentation layer delivers the user interface to the web browser. It handles all user interactions, form submissions, and real-time updates through API calls to the backend.
Separate dashboards are rendered for the patient, doctor, and pharmacist roles based on the authenticated user session.

Application Layer (Backend): Built using Node.js and PHP, the application layer processes all business logic, enforces role-based access control, handles API requests from the frontend, manages user sessions, and communicates with the database. This layer also manages the real-time chat functionality using WebSocket or a REST polling approach.

Data Layer (Database): Built using MySQL, the data layer stores all persistent system data including user accounts, patient health records, consultation logs, electronic prescriptions, pharmacy records, and referral appointments. The database is hosted on a local XAMPP server during the development and testing phases.
The database will be designed using a relational model in MySQL. The following core tables will form the database schema:
Stores user account details for all roles including name, email, hashed password, role (patient/doctor/pharmacist), and registration date.
Stores patient-specific profile information including date of birth, gender, address, and medical history summary.
Stores doctor-specific profile data including medical licence number, specialisation, and affiliated institution.
Stores pharmacist profile details including pharmacy name, registration number, and physical address.
Records each consultation session including the patient ID, doctor ID, consultation date, submitted symptoms, diagnosis notes, and consultation status.
Stores electronic prescriptions including prescription ID, consultation ID, medication name, dosage, frequency, duration, issuing doctor ID, assigned pharmacy ID, and prescription status.
Stores the full medical history of each patient, updated after every consultation by the attending doctor.
Records referral details for patients with ambiguous symptoms, including referred clinic name, appointment date, time, and referral reason.
Stores system-generated notifications sent to patients, doctors, and pharmacists for events such as new consultations, prescriptions, and appointment confirmations.
The following use case descriptions detail the key interactions between users and the system for the most critical functional requirements.
Use Case 1: Patient Requests a Consultation
The patient is registered and logged into the system.
1. Patient navigates to the consultation request page. 2. Patient fills in the symptom submission form
ng their complaints. 3. Patient submits the request. 4. The system assigns the request to an available doctor. 5. The doctor receives a notification of the new consultation request.
A consultation request is created and stored in the consultations table. The assigned doctor is notified.
If no doctor is currently available, the system queues the request and notifies the patient that they will be attended to shortly.
Use Case 2: Doctor Issues an Electronic Prescription
The doctor is logged in and has reviewed the patient's consultation and symptoms.

1. Doctor reviews the patient's submitted symptoms and medical history. 2. Doctor selects the option to generate a prescription. 3. Doctor enters medication name, dosage, frequency, and duration. 4. Doctor
selects the target pharmacy from the registered pharmacy list. 5. Doctor confirms and submits the prescription. 6. The system saves the prescription and transmits it to the selected pharmacy.
An electronic prescription is stored in the prescriptions table with a unique ID. The patient and pharmacist are both notified.
If the doctor classifies the symptoms as ambiguous, they activate the referral module instead of generating a prescription (see UC-03).
Use Case 3: Doctor Refers Patient for Physical Testing
Doctor Refers Patient to Nearest Clinic
The doctor has reviewed the patient's symptoms and determined that they are ambiguous and cannot be safely prescribed for remotely.

1. Doctor selects the referral option from the consultation interface. 2. Doctor enters the reason for referral, the recommended clinic, and a proposed appointment date and time. 3. Doctor confirms the referral. 4. The system saves the referral record and notifies the patient.
A referral record is created in the referrals table. The patient receives a notification with the clinic name, appointment date, and time.
If the patient cannot attend the proposed appointment time, they may contact the clinic directly using the contact details provided.

Chapter Four: System Design and Implementation

This chapter details the system design and implementation aspects of the Web-Based Telemedicine Platform with an Electronic Prescription Management System. It outlines the architectural design, software design specifications, and the development approach adopted to build a robust, secure, and user-friendly platform. The design principles are guided by the functional and non-functional requirements identified in the preceding chapters, aiming to address the critical gaps in healthcare accessibility and prescription management within the Zambian context.

The proposed system adopts a three-tier client-server architecture to ensure a clear separation of concerns, scalability, and maintainability. This architecture comprises a Presentation Layer (Frontend), an Application Layer (Backend), and a Data Layer (Database). This structure facilitates modular development, allowing different components to be developed and managed independently while ensuring seamless integration. The architectural design is visually represented in Figure 4.2.1.

This layer is responsible for the user interface and user interaction. It is built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React.js, providing distinct dashboards for patients, doctors, and pharmacists. This layer handles all user inputs, displays information, and communicates with the backend via API calls

Developed using Node.js and PHP, this layer encapsulates the business logic, manages user authentication and authorization (Role-Based Access Control - RBAC), processes API requests from the frontend, and handles session management. It also incorporates real-time chat functionality, essential for remote consultations.

This layer consists of a MySQL relational database, which serves as the persistent storage for all system data. This includes user accounts, patient health records, consultation logs, electronic prescriptions, pharmacy records, and referral appointments. During development and testing, the database is hosted on a local XAMPP server.
